candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Assignment, Delegation and Supervision
candidate.educational_objective: After delegated data collection reveals a new abnormal finding, the RN retains responsibility for assessment, clinical judgment, supervision, evaluation, and appropriate follow-up.

options.A: The UAP assumes responsibility for interpreting the abnormal result and deciding the clinical follow-up.
options.B: The RN must always repeat the heart rate personally before any other assessment or follow-up can occur.
options.C: The UAP should determine whether ECG testing or healthcare-provider notification is needed.
options.D: The RN evaluates the reported change, obtains additional assessment data as clinically indicated, and determines the appropriate follow-up.

candidate.rationale: NCSBN/ANA delegation guidance states that the licensed nurse retains responsibility for supervision and evaluation of delegated care. The delegatee is expected to communicate patient status and may not independently make decisions or modifications outside the delegated activity without consulting the licensed nurse. A newly abnormal vital sign therefore requires RN evaluation and clinical judgment; the RN may obtain additional assessment data as indicated, but no universal rule requires personally repeating every delegated measurement before any other action.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The licensed nurse remains responsible for supervision, follow-up, and evaluation; the delegatee must report patient status and not independently modify the activity or make decisions outside delegated authority. Jurisdictional rules still govern delegation.
candidate.source_locator: Licensed Nurse Responsibilities → communication; Right supervision and evaluation; NCSBN Delegation page → jurisdictional-law caveat.
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN) and American Nurses Association (ANA)

candidate.stem: A UAP reports a heart rate of 118/min for a previously stable client after the RN delegated routine vital-sign measurement. What responsibility remains with the RN?
